headline: LaLiga confirmed theft of fan data, while Samsung Securities reported a breach affecting 8,241 customers. The European Commission confirmed that its October attack exposed EU Academy users’ names and email addresses.

incidents.what: LaLiga confirmed that an intruder took personal data from one platform serving fans of the league and some clubs.
The hospital director said encrypted databases and disrupted phones and clinical systems forced three sites to postpone non-urgent care.
The Block estimated about $2 million in attacker proceeds and separately valued later withdrawals from Fusionist’s bridge reserves at about $3.7 million.
The brokerage confirmed that an intrusion into its customer feedback system exposed personal information, including some account and driver’s license numbers.
The Commission confirmed EU Academy users’ names and email addresses leaked in the October intrusion, and disabled public access to the platform.
South Korea’s privacy regulator opened an investigation; the utility confirmed exposure for 650,487 billing users and is treating 869,761 procurement users as potentially affected.
Snowys removed malicious code that may have captured customer details and passwords entered on its website.
The web agency confirmed unauthorized access to a client backup server and said some data offered for sale came from its backups.
Next said an intrusion at an online supplier exposed limited company data but found no evidence that its own systems or customer personal data were affected.
incidents.scale: No evidence of customer data exposure

incidents.what: Peninsula Energy said an incident at the Lance uranium project would temporarily affect operations and that its administrative systems were not breached.
Suzlon confirmed a cyber incident and notified CERT-In, without confirming Blackout’s claim or reporting impact on critical applications.
HD Hyundai Robotics said an intruder accessed a website server holding subscriber names, usernames, passwords described as encrypted, and contact details.
